body.statement:
In the multihomogeneous system used by \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), the query component has at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks and its binary-factor graph is simple. For a simple graph on at most two blocks every prescribed-indegree coefficient is at most \(1\); on at most three blocks it is at most \(2\); and on at most four blocks it is at most \(4\), with
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
If \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the coefficient is at most \(3\). Hence every finite queried-coordinate degree satisfies
\[
 d_e(G)\leq1\quad(n=3),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq2\quad(n=4),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq3\quad(n=5,\ |D\setminus T|\leq1),
\]
and \(d_e(G)\leq4\) when \(n=5\).
body.proof_tex:
For a finite simple graph \(H=(W,E_H)\) and a vector \(r=(r_v:v\in W)\) of nonnegative integers, define
\[
 c_H(r)=\left[\prod_{v\in W}X_v^{r_v}\right]
          \prod_{\{u,v\}\in E_H}(X_u+X_v).
\]
Choosing \(X_v\) from the factor indexed by \(\{u,v\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(v\). Therefore \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) having indegree vector \(r\). In particular it is zero unless
\[
 \sum_{v\in W}r_v=|E_H|,
 \qquad 0\leq r_v\leq\deg_H(v).
 \tag{1}
\]

If \(|W|\leq2\), simplicity gives at most one edge, and its orientation is fixed by its indegree vector. Thus \(c_H(r)\leq1\). If \(|W|\leq3\) and \(H\) is a forest, two distinct orientations with the same indegrees would have a nonempty balanced symmetric difference; following edges of that difference would produce a cycle, contrary to acyclicity. Hence the count is at most one. The only remaining graph is the triangle. Its two cyclic orientations both have indegree vector \((1,1,1)\), while every transitive orientation has a distinct labeled permutation of \((0,1,2)\). Hence the maximum on three blocks is two.

Now suppose \(|W|\leq4\). If \(|E_H|\leq4\), every connected component is a tree or there is exactly one unicyclic component: two independent cycle contributions in a simple graph on at most four vertices require at least five edges. In a tree attached to a cycle, the prescribed indegree at a leaf fixes its incident edge, and iterating from the leaves fixes every attached-tree edge. A cycle has at most its two cyclic orientations with the same remaining indegrees. Componentwise,
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2\qquad (|E_H|\leq4).
 \tag{2}
\]

For five edges, necessarily \(H=K_4\setminus\{1,2\}\). Directly expanding
\[
 P=(X_1+X_3)(X_1+X_4)(X_2+X_3)(X_2+X_4)(X_3+X_4)
\]
and fixing \((r_1,r_2)=(a,b)\in\{0,1,2\}^2\) gives the following maxima over the remaining two exponents:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
  &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
 a=0&1&2&1\\
 a=1&2&3&2\\
 a=2&1&2&1
 \end{array}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, choose the \(a\) factors among \(X_1+X_3,X_1+X_4\) that contribute \(X_1\), choose the \(b\) factors among \(X_2+X_3,X_2+X_4\) that contribute \(X_2\), and make either choice in \(X_3+X_4\); collecting equal exponent pairs gives (3). Thus every five-edge coefficient is at most three. When all four block capacities are positive, (1) forces a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\); the coefficient is three when the exponent two is at vertex \(3\) or \(4\), and two when it is at vertex \(1\) or \(2\).

For six edges, \(H=K_4\). The possible sorted exponent patterns satisfying (1) are
\[
 (0,0,3,3),\quad(0,1,2,3),\quad(0,2,2,2),
 \quad(1,1,1,3),\quad(1,1,2,2).
\]
The first has coefficient zero because the edge joining the two zero-exponent vertices has no endpoint from which a variable may be chosen. A labeled vector of type \((0,1,2,3)\) has one transitive orientation. In types \((0,2,2,2)\) and \((1,1,1,3)\), the edges incident to the extreme vertex are forced and the remaining triangle has its two cyclic orientations. Finally, for \(r=(1,1,2,2)\), condition on the factor \(X_1+X_2\). If it contributes \(X_1\), the factors on edges \(13\) and \(14\) must contribute \(X_3X_4\), after which the triangle on \(2,3,4\) has two cyclic choices. The case in which it contributes \(X_2\) is symmetric. Therefore
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{i<j}(X_i+X_j)=2+2=4.
 \tag{4}
\]
This proves the four-block maximum and its attainment.

It remains to connect these counts to the SEM bound. In the square subsystem selected for \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), variables are blocked by child vertex. A rooted arborescence has one root, so there are at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks. The displayed formula for \(F_{ij}\) has degree at most one in the block for child \(i\), degree at most one in the block for child \(j\), and degree zero in every other block. An unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\) supplies at most its single residual \(F_{ij}\), so the binary-factor graph is simple. By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\), the relevant B\'ezout coefficient is the orientation count just bounded.

For \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the arborescence and excess budget give \(|D|\leq5\). A selected square subsystem therefore has at most five equations, hence at most five binary factors after unary factors are removed. With at most four binary factors, (2) gives the stronger bound two. With five binary factors there is no unary factor, all four blocks occur, and their positive capacities sum to five. The only capacity pattern is therefore a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\), and (3) bounds its coefficient by three. Combining this with the two-, three-, and four-block bounds proves all displayed consequences for \(d_e(G)\).
